# Core Loop and Frame Lifecycle

> **Draft chapter map.** Explain how the engine converts continuous platform events into coordinated simulation, presentation, and service work.

## Time Is an Engine Service

- Establish that “a frame” is a presentation opportunity, not a universal clock for every subsystem.
- Separate real time, scaled game time, and fixed simulation time before introducing implementation details.

### Fixed and Variable Work

- Explain why physics and deterministic gameplay need a stable cadence while cameras, UI, and visual effects can update at frame rate.
- Compare accumulator-based fixed stepping with naive frame-time simulation.

#### Interpolation and Catch-Up Policy

- Explain the visual role of interpolation and the safety role of bounded catch-up.
- Foreshadow the explicit policies for pause, slow frames, and time debt.

## Overlapped Frame Execution

- Show the conceptual overlap between the game side preparing one frame and the render side presenting another.
- Explain that overlap is a latency/throughput trade-off, not an unconditional performance win.

### Pacing, Backpressure, and Presentation

- Describe the display, the GPU queue, and the engine as separate pacing influences.
- Establish bounded queues and named latency budgets as the alternative to unbounded frame accumulation.

#### Adaptive Quality as a Control Loop

- Introduce feedback-driven decisions such as dynamic resolution without committing to a particular algorithm.
- Connect quality changes to measured budgets rather than one-off feature switches.

## Lifecycle Events Are First-Class Work

- Explain why resize, focus, minimize, device loss, and shutdown cannot be treated as ordinary gameplay events.

### Pausing, Resuming, and World Transitions

- Separate pausing simulation from freezing the entire application.
- Explain how a responsive UI and loading experience can coexist with a paused or changing World.

#### Graceful Teardown

- Outline the order in which work is stopped, resources are released, and threads are joined.
- Emphasize recoverable failure paths over process-wide assumptions.
